The test image shows a corn leaf with:
1. One prominent round/oval, white-tan spot (~1/4 inch) in the lower portion
2. Some light yellowish streaking along the veins in the upper area

Top candidates: **Holcus_spot** (round, tan-white spots with margins) and **Eyespot** (small circular spots with halos). Let me view reference images.

The Holcus_spot reference images are a near-perfect match — the bottom-left panel shows the exact same round white/tan spot on a green corn leaf in the same setting as the test image. Let me view more references to confirm and rule out other candidates.

Neither Anthracnose nor Common rust match — they show elongated/dark lesions and brick-red pustules respectively, quite different from the test image.

**Analysis summary:**
- **Test image**: Single, prominent round/circular white-tan spot (~1/4 inch) on an otherwise healthy green corn leaf. Background shows small plants and soil.
- **Holcus_spot reference**: The bottom-left panel of the Holcus_spot collage is virtually identical to the test image — same leaf texture, same round white spot, same background setting with small plant visible. Description matches perfectly: "Round or elliptical, tan to white spots 1/8 to 1/4 inch in diameter with red to brown margins."
- **Eyespot**: Shows many small yellowish spots with clear halos — too numerous and different in color.
- **Gray_leaf_spot**: Rectangular lesions — wrong shape entirely.
- **Stewarts_wilt**: Young plant wilting — completely different.
- **Common_rust**: Brick-red pustules — no match.
- **Anthracnose**: Elongated dark lesions with setae — no match.

The round, isolated white-tan spot is a classic Holcus spot lesion (caused by *Pseudomonas syringae* pv. *syringae*).
